text: Formula Context: Bonding Coordination Number Identifying atoms “bonded” key determining coordination number (CN). crystract implements several robust, geometric, mathematical approaches: minimum_distance: Defines custom distance cutoff central atom ii: dicut=(1+δ)dimin  d_i^\text{cut} = (1+\delta) d_i^\text{min}   , dimind_i^\text{min} shortest distance atom ii atom, δ\delta tolerance parameter (default 0.1). brunner: Identifies bonds finding largest gap reciprocal distances. Matches pymatgen.analysis.local_env.BrunnerNNReciprocal. econ: Uses Hoppe’s iterative method calculate Effective Coordination Numbers, weighting neighbor contributions exponentially distance. voronoi: Performs 3D Voronoi tessellation find neighbors sharing face. Note: crystract calculates faces using Delaunay dual. Results may slightly differ exact Voronoi tessellation implementations (like Voro++) due geometric handling degenerate, co-planar vertices. crystal_nn: sophisticated approach combining Voronoi solid angles, ionic radii distance cutoffs, electronegativity weights. Let’s run algorithm demonstrate:

CrystalNN bonds_crystal_nn <- crystal_nn(distances, atomic_coordinates, expanded_coords, unit_cell_metrics)  cat("Minimum Distance found", nrow(bonds_min), "bonds.\n") #> Minimum Distance found 14 bonds. cat("CrystalNN found", nrow(bonds_crystal_nn), "bonds.\n") #> CrystalNN found 36 bonds.  # Calculate integer neighbor counts based on the bonded pairs (e.g., using CrystalNN) neighbor_counts <- calculate_neighbor_counts(bonds_crystal_nn) print("CrystalNN Neighbor Counts:") #> [1] "CrystalNN Neighbor Counts:" print(neighbor_counts) #>      Atom CoordinationNumber #>    <char>              <int> #> 1:  Sr1_2                 12 #> 2:  Sr2_2                 15 #> 3:  Si1_2                  9

text: function designed facilitate analysis based crystallographic site symmetry. particularly useful analyzing complex structures like clathrates different atoms perform distinct structural roles based site symmetry. function works : Creating full Wyckoff label (e.g., "4c", "24k") combining WyckoffMultiplicity WyckoffSymbol columns atomic_coordinates table. title: Filter Data by Wyckoff Symbol — filter_by_wyckoff_symbol
code:
cif_file <- system.file("extdata", "1590946.cif", package = "crystract") if (file.exists(cif_file)) {   # 1. Perform a standard analysis to get bond and coordinate tables   cif_content <- read_cif_files(cif_file)[[1]]   atoms <- extract_atomic_coordinates(cif_content)   metrics <- extract_unit_cell_metrics(cif_content)   sym_ops <- extract_symmetry_operations(cif_content)   full_cell <- apply_symmetry_operations(atoms, sym_ops, metrics)   super_cell <- expand_transformed_coords(full_cell)   dists <- calculate_distances(atoms, super_cell, metrics)   bonds <- minimum_distance(dists)    # 2. Mock Wyckoff sites since 1590946 doesn't explicitly declare them   atoms[, WyckoffSymbol := "c"]   atoms[, WyckoffMultiplicity := 4]    print("Original atomic coordinates showing Wyckoff sites:")   print(atoms[, .(Label, WyckoffSymbol, WyckoffMultiplicity)])    filtered_bonds <- filter_by_wyckoff_symbol(     data_table = bonds,     atomic_coordinates = atoms,     atom_col = "Atom1",     wyckoff_symbols = "4c"   )    cat("
Number of bonds in original table:", nrow(bonds), "
")   cat("Number of bonds after filtering for '4c' site:", nrow(filtered_bonds), "
") } #> [1] "Original atomic coordinates showing Wyckoff sites:" #>     Label WyckoffSymbol WyckoffMultiplicity #>    <char>        <char>               <num> #> 1:    Sr1             c                   4 #> 2:    Sr2             c                   4 #> 3:    Si1             c                   4 #>  #> Number of bonds in original table: 14  #> Number of bonds after filtering for '4c' site: 14
